verdicts.raw:
The model treats every pair of operations across all jobs and within the same job as conflicting, as if all 19 operations ran on a single machine. The problem does not say that. It states that only operations assigned to the same machine conflict, and it gives example pairs such as (1,3) with (2,4), and (1,1) with (3,2). The machine assignments are not given in the text, so the true conflict set is unknown.

The all-pairs choice is a serious distortion. The resulting makespan would be at least the sum of all processing times, which is 5 + 24 + 30 + 42 = 101. The intended job-shop makespan is far lower, since job 3 alone has a length of 42 and the intended answer is probably in the 40s to 50s.

The text also hints at the conflict pairs. The pair (1,3) and (2,4) has a "start at least 4 units after" gap, which matches the 4-unit duration of (2,4). The pair (1,1) and (3,2) has a gap of 7, which matches the 7-unit duration of (1,1). These pairs suggest particular machine sharing, which the model ignores.

The solver status is a timeout with no objective value, so there is no solution to check. The model is wrong in structure regardless.
